_comment: Sovereign source of truth. No digest may be hardcoded anywhere else.
Digests marked sha256:0000... require an authenticated dhi.io login to resolve;
see SETUP-ENVIRONMENTS.md step 7. Every other digest was resolved live on
2026-08-18 and should be re-checked with `make -f Ops.mk verify-pins`.
CODEOWNERS puts this file under @infrashift/security-admins: a `track` widening
is a one-character edit that silently converts every future release from a
reviewed decision into an automated bump.

ory.note: All four Ory services release in lockstep off a shared tag. A partial bump is a bug; drift-upstream.yml must propose all four together.

keto-cue.note: First-party (ADR-008). keto-cue publishes no release tags yet, so `ref` is the Go pseudo-version of the pinned commit (committer time in UTC, then the 12-char commit prefix) -- the module version `go version -m` stamps from the shallow checkout. The track admits only that shape, so drift-upstream.sh finds no tag to propose and every bump is a reviewed manual edit of commit and ref together. When keto-cue starts tagging releases, replace the track with one for its release line in its own reviewed PR.

chit.note: First-party (ADR-008). Chit publishes no release tags yet, so `ref` is the Go pseudo-version of the pinned commit (committer time in UTC, then the 12-char commit prefix). The track admits only that shape, so drift-upstream.sh finds no tag to propose and every bump is a reviewed manual edit of commit and ref together. When Chit starts tagging releases, replace the track with one for its release line in its own reviewed PR.

nats.shortCommitNote: goreleaser stamps {{.ShortCommit}}, whose length is git's DYNAMIC abbreviation for the full repo. Verified empirically: the released v2.14.5 binary embeds 9 characters. It cannot be derived from our build, because fetch-source.sh makes a --depth 1 clone and git then abbreviates to the 7-char minimum. Pinning it as data is the only way to reproduce the vendor's binary; drift PRs must update it alongside `commit`.
nats.note: Moved up from the 2.11 line the user ran previously. Upstream pins GOTOOLCHAIN and uses -trimpath, so this is the one service where a byte-identical cross-check is realistic.

dapr.note: One source repo produces all three images. Moved up from 1.14.4, which is outside Dapr's N-2 support window. Scheduler is included because from 1.15+ actor reminders and workflows require it. v1.18.9 (lightweight tag on 7b4c3832) replaced the v1.18.4 pin on 2026-10-28; the earlier untagged release-1.18 pin, taken because v1.18.3 vendored etcd 3.5.30 (GO-2026-6107, GO-2026-6114), is superseded by tagged releases. ref must be OCI-tag-safe: build-leg.sh interpolates it into DEST_TAG=pr-<n>-<ref>-<arch>, and a '+' there is rejected by the registry grammar, which surfaces only as buildah exit 125.

web-ui.note: The compiled web UI. A source build without Node and pnpm has no UI (`builtinassets` embeds web/ui/static, which only `make assets` populates), and upstream publishes this tarball for exactly that case -- its Makefile honours PREBUILT_ASSETS_STATIC_DIR. Its paths are static/..., the shape scripts/package_assets.sh writes. sha256 for v3.15.1 copied 2026-10-28 from the release's sha256sums.txt and confirmed against the downloaded tarball. Prometheus does not sign release assets, so this hash IS the trust claim. A drift bump moves the URL but cannot re-pin the hash; scripts/fetch-assets.sh refuses a URL that does not name the release being built.

prometheus.note: Initial pin, the newest release (2026-09-24). Track is the 3.15 minor line, like nats. Upstream's .promu.yml builds with Go 1.27; go.mod only requires 1.26.0, so our go1.26 toolchain builds it with GOTOOLCHAIN=local (no toolchain download) and the cross-check is best-effort.

loki.shortCommitNote: Loki's Makefile stamps Revision from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, git's DYNAMIC abbreviation for the full repo. Verified on the vendor's v3.7.9 binary (`loki -version`, 2026-10-28): revision d3b4a2f7, 8 characters. drift-upstream.sh proposed d3b4a2f76b (10) from its own clone, so the vendor binary, not the clone, is the reference. fetch-source.sh's --depth 1 clone would abbreviate to 7, so it is pinned as data; drift PRs must update it alongside `commit`.
loki.note: Initial pin, the newest release (2026-09-17). v3.7.8 is a lightweight tag on 09e6ce2f. Track is the 3.7 minor line, like prometheus and nats. go.mod requires go 1.26.5 and upstream's cmd/loki/Dockerfile builds with 1.26.6, the patch our go1.26 toolchain pin carried at the time; it has since moved to 1.26.9 (see toolchains.go1.26.goVersion).

seaweedfs.shortCommitNote: Upstream's container build stamps COMMIT from `git rev-parse --short HEAD`, git's DYNAMIC abbreviation for the full repo: 9 characters on 4.48 (`weed version`: "version 30GB 4.48 530be3e37 linux amd64", 2026-10-08). fetch-source.sh's --depth 1 clone would abbreviate to 7, so it is pinned as data; drift PRs must update it alongside `commit`. 4.51 exception (2026-10-28): the vendor's 4.51 image reports ffa87c25f, one commit past the 4.51 tag on master (ffa87c25 changes only three .github/workflows files, so the Go sources are identical). We build the tag and stamp what we built, 153ab668c; the vendor revision string will differ on this release.
seaweedfs.note: Initial pin, the newest release (2026-09-28). Tags carry no leading v (4.48, 4.47, ...), and every release bumps the minor, so the track is the whole 4.x line. go.mod requires go 1.26.6, the patch our go1.26 toolchain pin carried at the time; it has since moved to 1.26.9 (see toolchains.go1.26.goVersion).

prometheus-nats-exporter.note: Initial pin, the newest release (2026-08-19). v0.20.2 is a lightweight tag on 6d32406b. No shortCommit: goreleaser passes -X main.commit={{.ShortCommit}}, but main.go declares only `version`, so the vendor binary stamps no commit and there is nothing to reproduce. Track is the 0.20 minor line.

archive.note: The sha256 is the `hash valkey-9.1.3.tar.gz sha256 ...` line of valkey-io/valkey-hashes (README at cbac0d5b, 2026-11-04), a repository separate from the source. Confirmed 2026-11-15: the downloaded archive has that sha256, and its file tree is identical to the tree of commit 29173b67 (diff -r, no .gitattributes export-ignore). Valkey does not sign its tags or archives, so this hash is the independent check on the commit.

valkey.note: Initial pin, the newest Valkey release (9.1.3, 2026-10-26; lightweight tag on 29173b67). Upgrade urgency SECURITY: it fixes GHSA-f4q9-j22m-xqq9, a heap buffer overflow in cluster Pub/Sub message construction (#5030). Track is the 9.1 minor line, like nats. Native build (ADR-010): compiled on UBI with TLS, no vendor binary comparison.

archive.note: NOT a vendor-published hash: PgBouncer publishes a sha256 only for its `make dist` tarball (https://www.pgbouncer.org/downloads/files/1.26.1/pgbouncer-1.26.1.tar.gz.sha256 = 00886a2994b4844cd37110970df777772cfc42a74c400522c82fba509a3f42d9), and that tarball is the commit tree plus five generated autotools files (configure, config.guess, config.sub, install-sh, lib/usual/config.h.in), so scripts/fetch-archive.sh, which requires identical trees, cannot use it. This sha256 is GitHub's tag archive, computed by us on 2026-11-15 (TOFU). Checked by hand on 2026-11-15: the vendor tarball has the published sha256, and its tree minus those five generated files is identical to the tree of commit f03e9bf2 (diff -r); the GitHub archive's tree is identical to the commit's. No hashSource: the vendor publishes none for this file. A drift bump moves the URL; take the new sha256 from the new GitHub archive and repeat the by-hand comparison with the vendor tarball before merging.

pgbouncer.note: Initial pin, the newest PgBouncer release (1.26.1, 2026-10-14). The ref is the vendor's git tag, pgbouncer_1_26_1 (an annotated, unsigned tag on f03e9bf2), so scripts/fetch-source.sh can check that the tag names the pinned commit; it is also the image version and the release tag. libusual is vendored in lib/ as a plain tree (no .gitmodules). Track is the 1.26 minor line. Native build (ADR-010): compiled on UBI with OpenSSL, no vendor binary comparison.

go1.26.note: Also the donor for /usr/share/zoneinfo, which ubi9-micro does not ship. goVersion is the image's own GOLANG_VERSION, recorded so a reviewer can see the compiler patch without pulling the image; scripts/drift-upstream.sh re-pins the digests when the rolling tag moves and rewrites goVersion from the new image's config. 1.26.9 (2026-10-13) clears GO-2026-6603/6605/6607/6608/6610/6611/6612/6613, the net/http, crypto/tls and net/textproto advisories published 2026-10-08 that 1.26.6 carried. 1.26.10 re-pinned 2026-10-28 with the ubi9-minimal base refresh, so the full rebuild that base change triggers does not compile on a superseded patch release. 1.26.11 (released 2026-11-10, re-pinned 2026-11-14) carries security fixes to cgo, the go command, the compiler, the linker and net/http (GO-2026-6859, which govulncheck reported in Chit's CI on 1.26.10).

ubi9-micro.note: VERIFIED 2026-08-18: ships NO CA trust bundle, NO tzdata, and NO UID 1001 in /etc/passwd. It DOES have bash, coreutils and glibc, so RUN works. Registry path is trusted-base-images, not trusted-base-oci-images (the sibling's directory name differs from its git remote). arm64 is published as arm64/v8; always pin by digest.

ubi9-minimal.note: Donor for /etc/pki/ca-trust/extracted/pem/tls-ca-bundle.pem only. Assert the copied bundle is >100000 bytes so a truncated one fails loudly. Since 2026-11-14 also the RUNTIME base of the package-track image postgresql17 (ADR-009), whose Containerfile upgrades it from the signed UBI repositories before it installs anything.

pgdg17-el9.name: PostgreSQL Global Development Group (PGDG), PostgreSQL 17 for EL9
pgdg17-el9.note: Chosen 2026-11-14 because UBI9 AppStream has no PostgreSQL 17: no server package and no `postgresql` module stream (its modules.yaml lists maven, nginx, nodejs, php, redis and ruby only; the only PostgreSQL RPMs are the 13 client and its private libs). See ADR-009. PGDG signs each architecture with its own key: the x86_64 RPMs and repomd.xml with 40BCA2B408B40D20, the aarch64 ones with 177B343BB9738825. Both keys were fetched from keyUrl on 2026-11-14 (TOFU: neither is on keyserver.ubuntu.com); every pinned RPM and both repomd.xml.asc signatures verified against them. scripts/build-leg.sh refuses a key file whose sha256 or primary fingerprint differs from these values, and `make -f Ops.mk verify-package-pins` compares the live keyUrl with the committed copy, so a PGDG key rotation becomes a reviewed PR.

traefik.reason: Placeholder digests resolved 2026-08-24 with an authenticated dhi.io login (regctl manifest head, index digest). DHI repoints 3-debian13 itself, so the tag string never changes and only the digest moves; track is therefore an exact match.

postgres.reason: Initial pin, runtime + dev, PostgreSQL 16. Exact tags rather than a regex range: DHI repoints the tag itself, so only the digest moves, and drift-upstream proposes it. The PostgreSQL 17 pair (runtime17/dev17, tags 17-debian and 17-debian-dev, added 2026-09-15) was removed 2026-11-14: HALO and Chit, its only consumers, moved to the postgresql17 package-track image (PR #55), which replaces it. The 16 pair stays because ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack still pins trusted/postgres 16 by digest; remove this entry, and waiver EXC-2026-0034 with it, once that consumer moves. Removing the variants does not delete the images already published to GHCR.

nexus3.reason: Tracks the 3.90 patch line only; 3.91.0-ubi and 3.91.1-ubi already exist upstream, so a naive newest-tag check would jump a minor on its first run. Trust class none: public Docker Hub image with unsigned BuildKit attestations only. Onboarded in `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml -- a ~700MB JVM image will very likely quarantine.

notation.trustedIdentity: x509.subject: CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA Signing,O=Microsoft Corporation,L=Redmond,ST=Washington,C=US
notation.note: Root pinned by TOFU on 2026-09-11 from Microsoft's PKI endpoint; SHA-256 fingerprint 23:FF:E2:B8:BD:B9:A1:71:15:15:D4:CF:FD:A0:4B:C7:F7:93:D5:13:C7:6C:24:3F:10:20:50:7D:86:69:B7:DB, valid to 2047-02-17. The signing leaf (CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA Signing, expires 2027-10-31) chains via CN=Microsoft SCD Products RSA CA. Identity is pinned to the leaf subject because the root alone would trust every Microsoft product signature. Verified locally with notation v1.3.2 at level strict on 2026-09-11; a wrong root, a wrong identity and an out-of-scope registry each failed as expected.

mssql.reason: Pin moved 2026-09-15 from 2025-CU8-GDR1-rhel-10 (17.0.4085.5, sha256:54b58c3a) to 2025-CU9-rhel-10 (17.0.5005.3), the manifest 2025-latest now resolves to. Same repository, same RHEL 10 base, same bare amd64 manifest shape, Notary signature still present as an OCI referrer. This is the FIRST observed move of this rolling tag and it confirms the shape the initial pin predicted. Initial pin was SQL Server 2025 on the RHEL 10 base (mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/rhel/server, not the Ubuntu mssql/server repo) to match the repo's UBI posture. Rolling tag: Microsoft repoints 2025-latest on every CU and GDR, and a CU regex track would be a trap because `sort -V` orders 2025-CU8-GDR1-rhel-10 BEFORE 2025-CU8-rhel-10, so drift-upstream.sh would never propose a GDR security release. Track is therefore the exact tag and only the digest moves. Note this move goes GDR -> CU, which a CU-ordered track would also have mishandled. Trust class notation: the image carries a Notary Project signature as an OCI referrer, chained to Microsoft Supply Chain RSA Root CA 2022, which we vendor and verify against with the signing identity pinned. There is no cosign signature and no SBOM or provenance referrer, so no attestations are required of this class. Still `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml; CU9 is newer than the CU8-GDR1 it replaces, so the finding count should not rise.
mssql.note: amd64 ONLY, and a BARE manifest: the tag resolves to a single application/vnd.docker.distribution.manifest.v2+json with no index. Microsoft supports x86-64 hosts only and states emulation is untested. scripts/manifest-platforms.sh derives the platform set from the config os/arch for this shape. Runtime config: user mssql, port 1433, entrypoint /opt/mssql/bin/launch_sqlservr.sh, no declared volumes (data lives under /var/opt/mssql; mount it). The container starts only with ACCEPT_EULA=Y and a password supplied via the MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD environment variable at run time; MSSQL_PID defaults to developer and selecting a production edition asserts that the consumer holds a licence. The SQL build number is not in the tag; read the com.microsoft.version label from the evidence. The notation signature is an OCI referrer in the image's own repository; the mirror copies it with --referrers, and the first run's upstream-referrers.json should list artifactType application/vnd.cncf.notary.signature.

whoami.reason: Traefik's whoami echo server, the test backend infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack's sm-ingress runs behind the edge; it ran docker.io/traefik/whoami:latest. Pinned to v1.12.0, the release :latest resolves to on 2026-09-30 (same index digest). Track is the v1 release line: whoami is a stateless test fixture with no data or config contract, so a minor bump carries nothing a patch-only track would protect, and the regex excludes the per-arch (-amd64/-arm64/-armv7) and two-part rolling (v1.12) tags. Three platforms, not two: the upstream index carries linux/arm/v7, and a mirror copies the whole index, so the declared set must include it or PLATFORM_SET_MISMATCH denies. Trust class none: no cosign signature and no OCI referrers, only unsigned BuildKit attestation manifests inside the index. A scratch image holding one static Go binary with no USER, so it reports root (RUNTIME_RUNS_AS_ROOT, a warning); the binary needs no privilege except a port below 1024, so consumers run it as a non-root uid on an unprivileged port (--user 65532:65532 --port=8080, proven 2026-09-30). Onboarded in `observe` until the day-one CVE triage lands in exceptions.yaml; expect Go standard-library findings from the toolchain it was built with.

ollama.reason: Initial pin for HALO's NVIDIA GPU nodes (ADR-011, accepted 2026-11-15): the DHI Debian 13 CUDA variant, verified with the DHI key, UID 65532, CUDA 13.2 or later on the host driver. The owner accepted the Debian base, the lag behind upstream (DHI 0.40.13, Ollama 0.40.16 on 2026-11-15) and NVIDIA only; AMD (ROCm) needs a new decision. The track allows only 0.40 patch releases of the debian13-cuda variant (not -dev, -fips or the Alpine CPU variant); a new Ollama minor is a reviewed track change. Onboarded in observe.

crosscheck.note: The -distroless tag, NOT the bare v26.2.0 tag. The bare tag is the Alpine/musl CGO_ENABLED=1 -tags=sqlite,hsm,json1 build (User 10000, 3.6MB base layer) and is not comparable to ours. Ory's cosign signature has Cert:false/Chain:false and no published public key, so we pin by digest and do not claim to verify it.

kratos.reason: Initial pin. No official UBI-based Ory image exists; built from source onto ubi9-micro.

hydra.reason: Initial pin. Note the module path carries /v2. Hydra has no .docker/Dockerfile-build (it has Dockerfile-local-build); the ldflags paths come from .goreleaser.yml.

build.note: Keto's .docker/Dockerfile-build sets CGO_ENABLED=1, but that is the dev build. The released -distroless image is CGO-free and keto's sqlite driver is modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go), so CGO is not needed. Verify `keto migrate up` works before trusting this.

keto-cue is a fork of Ory Keto v26.2.0 and keeps the module path github.com/ory/keto, so the ldflags symbols are Keto's. -tags=json1 and CGO_ENABLED=0 are the flags of Ory's static release build (ory/xgoreleaser build.tmpl.yml); keto-cue's .goreleaser.yml includes that template, and its code declares no sqlite or hsm tag. The SQLite driver is modernc.org/sqlite (pure Go). -trimpath is added: there is no vendor binary to match flags with, and it removes the build path from the binary. The CUE base schema is go:embed-ed, so the image needs no runtime CUE file; operators mount their own namespaces.cue.

firstParty.reason: keto-cue is infrashift's own fork of Ory Keto with a CUE schema language. infrashift is its only publisher and releases no container image of it, so no vendor binary exists to cross-check against.

keto-cue.reason: Initial pin for HALO (P-TSC-2): keto-cue replaces Ory Keto as the relation store. Onboarded in observe.

build.noVersionSymbol: Chit declares no version variable in any package (cmd/chitd and cmd/chit-reconcile have none; internal/api/system.go returns a literal), so there is no symbol to stamp. The module version and vcs.revision are in the Go build info, and the image labels carry the pinned commit.
build.note: One image, as chit's own deploy/Containerfile ships it: chitd (server) plus chit-reconcile, the one-shot job that pushes auth/*.cue grants into Keto, so the job and the server read the same CUE from the same commit. auth/ ships at /etc/chit/auth (CHIT_COMMANDS_CUE_DIR) and migrations/*.sql at /usr/share/chit/migrations for a golang-migrate job; Chit has no migrate binary. chit-mcp and chit-claude are client tools and are not built. CGO_ENABLED=0 as upstream; GOWORK=off as chit's Makefile, because go.work also names clients/chit-tui. go.mod asks for go 1.26.10 and names toolchain go1.26.11; GOTOOLCHAIN=local ignores the toolchain line and the pinned go1.26 compiler (1.26.11) builds it. Attachments (pkg/imagecheck with golang.org/x/image, internal/blob as a hand-written SigV4 S3 client) and the membership hook (golang.org/x/oauth2 clientcredentials) are pure Go and need no cgo, no runtime file and no new directory: the blob store is a remote S3 endpoint (SeaweedFS) set by CHIT_S3_ENDPOINT, and both features are off when their URL is empty.

firstParty.reason: Chit is infrashift's own chat service. infrashift is its only publisher and releases no container image of it, so no vendor binary exists to cross-check against.

chit.reason: Bump for HALO to Chit main 5b026fa9 (PR #10 merge, P-CHIT-8): rate limits per principal for on-behalf-of requests and an aggregate bucket per allowlisted client, set by CHIT_RATE_LIMIT_USER_PER_SECOND/_BURST and CHIT_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_PER_SECOND/_BURST, with Retry-After on 429; no go.mod, migration, port or file change. Previous bump to 1af19e66 (PR #9 merge): file attachments stored in S3-compatible SeaweedFS (P-CHIT-5, migration 000009) and the membership policy hook (P-CHIT-2), plus scoped tags (migration 000008). Initial pin for HALO (P-TSC-3): Chit holds HALO's Channels and Messages. Onboarded in observe.

build.note: Oathkeeper stamps into package x, NOT driver/configuration. Confirmed from .goreleaser.yml at v26.2.0. Getting this wrong is silent: the binary compiles and reports `dev`.

oathkeeper.reason: Initial pin. Upstream's .docker/Dockerfile-build has a bug (COPY oryx/go.sum proto/go.sum); we do not use it.

nats.archNote: Upstream also publishes arm/v6, arm/v7, 386, ppc64le, s390x and loong64. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Flags mirror upstream .goreleaser.yml: -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, -w (not -s -w). serverVersion takes the tag; gitCommit takes goreleaser's .ShortCommit. GOTOOLCHAIN deliberately diverges from upstream's go1.26.5: it is `local`, the pinned go1.26 toolchain image's own compiler (see Containerfiles/nats.Containerfile).

crosscheck.note: Second, independent anchor: the official image does not compile the binary, it downloads the GitHub release tarball and verifies these sha256 values inline in nats-docker/2.14.x/alpine3.22/Dockerfile. Both were confirmed to match on 2026-08-18, and the binary inside the official image is byte-identical to the released tarball. Re-confirmed for v2.14.9 on 2026-10-28: the hashes equal both the release's SHA256SUMS and nats-docker 2027d0acef (2.14.x/alpine3.22/Dockerfile at NATS_SERVER=2.14.9), and the nats-server in each 2.14.9-alpine3.22 child is byte-identical to its tarball's (amd64 and arm64). The vendor binary embeds the 9-char short commit 9ece58841. TIER DOWNGRADED from flag-matched to best-effort after empirical testing: we reproduced every observable build input -- Go 1.26.5, identical dep set, -trimpath, CGO_ENABLED=0, GOAMD64=v1, DefaultGODEBUG, mod=v2.14.5, vcs.revision/time/modified=false, and the 9-char short commit -- and the binary still differs. Whatever remains is not visible in `go version -m`. Do not treat a NATS mismatch as alarming until someone identifies the residual input.

runtime.configNote: Ours, not upstream's. nats-docker ships a cluster block with hardcoded credentials ruser/T0pS3cr3t. All three ports are >1024 so non-root binding is fine.

nats.reason: Initial pin on the 2.14 line, moved up from the 2.11-alpine image previously in use.

daprd.archNote: Upstream index is a Docker manifest list that also contains windows/amd64 and linux/arm/v7. Cross-check pins per-platform tags so extraction never depends on runtime manifest-list resolution.

runtime.userNote: Upstream runs 65532:65532 and the Dapr Helm chart pins runAsUser: 65532. We use 1001 per repo convention, so a Helm deployment needs an override. The /daprd compat symlink exists because the injector may emit command: ["/daprd"].
runtime.portNote: Ports are from documentation, not from the pinned source. VERIFY against cmd/daprd options before relying on them.

daprd.reason: Initial pin. Moved up from 1.14.4, which is outside Dapr's N-2 support window.

crosscheck.note: daprio/placement is the dedicated single-binary image. daprio/dapr is the kitchen-sink image carrying all six control-plane binaries and is the wrong cross-check source.

runtime.portNote: From documentation. VERIFY against cmd/placement options.

dapr-placement.reason: Initial pin. Built from the same source checkout as daprd and dapr-scheduler; sources.dapr.lockstep prevents drift.

runtime.portNote: From documentation. VERIFY against cmd/scheduler options.
runtime.volumeNote: The scheduler keeps an embedded etcd store; confirm the default data dir at the pinned tag before relying on this path.

dapr-scheduler.reason: Initial pin. Required from Dapr 1.15+ for actor reminders and workflows; the user is migrating from 1.14 where it did not exist.

prometheus.archNote: Upstream's index also carries arm/v7, ppc64le, riscv64 and s390x. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Binaries, tags and ldflags are upstream's .promu.yml at v3.15.0. Version takes the ref WITHOUT the leading v (promu stamps {{.Version}} from the VERSION file, 3.15.0). BuildDate is the source commit date, not wall-clock, so a rerun stamps the same string. promtool ships on purpose: it is the image's only HTTP client (ubi9-micro has no curl), and consumers use `promtool check healthy --http.config.file` as a health check that can present a client certificate.

crosscheck.note: Upstream's own image (busybox base, USER nobody, ENTRYPOINT /bin/prometheus), per-platform children of the v3.15.1 index sha256:fa330227... resolved 2026-10-28. Unsigned, so trust class none. best-effort: upstream compiles with Go 1.27 and we use 1.26, so a mismatch is expected and proves nothing.

runtime.configNote: CMD and /etc/prometheus/prometheus.yml are upstream's (documentation/examples/prometheus.yml, from the pinned source tree), so the image runs standalone exactly as quay.io/prometheus/prometheus does. Real deployments mount their own config, and a web config for TLS.

prometheus.reason: Initial pin. No usable UBI-based Prometheus exists: Red Hat's registry.redhat.io/openshift4/ose-prometheus-rhel9 needs an entitled, authenticated pull and ships OpenShift's fork on the OCP release train (v4.22), not upstream; DHI's is Debian-based. Built from source onto ubi9-micro. Onboarded in observe per adding-an-upstream.md; moved to enforce 2026-10-01 after the first review (PR #25) came back clean on both arches: allow=true, blocking=0, waived=0, 6 recorded (non-blocking), so no exception was needed. Consumer: infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack terraform/live/prometheus.

loki.archNote: Upstream's index also carries arm/v7. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Tags and ldflags are upstream's Makefile at v3.7.8 (GO_FLAGS: -s -w, -tags netgo, CGO_ENABLED=0; VPREFIX pkg/util/build). Version is the ref WITHOUT the leading v (tools/image-tag strips it; the vendor binary reports 3.7.8). Revision is the pinned shortCommit. Branch is HEAD (the vendor's CI reports release-3.7.x, which is not pinned data). BuildDate is the source commit date, not wall-clock. -trimpath is ours. logcli ships on purpose: it is the operator's query client, and consumers run it from this signed image rather than an unpinned download.

crosscheck.note: Upstream's own image (distroless/static:nonroot, USER 10001, ENTRYPOINT /usr/bin/loki), per-platform children of the 3.7.9 index sha256:0db216b6... resolved 2026-10-28. best-effort: upstream builds without -trimpath and stamps a wall-clock BuildDate and root@buildkitsandbox, so a byte mismatch is expected and proves nothing even on the same Go patch.

runtime.configNote: CMD and /etc/loki/local-config.yaml are upstream's (cmd/loki/loki-docker-config.yaml, from the pinned source tree), so the image runs standalone exactly as docker.io/grafana/loki does. Real deployments mount their own config.

loki.reason: Initial pin. No usable UBI-based Loki exists: Red Hat's logging-loki-rhel9 is an entitled, authenticated pull on the OpenShift Logging release train; the vendor image is distroless/static (Debian). Built from source onto ubi9-micro. Onboarded in observe per adding-an-upstream.md. Licence AGPL-3.0-only (LICENSING.md; pkg/ subfolders Apache-2.0); unmodified and run internally. Consumer: infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack terraform/live/loki (PLAN-Logging.md Part A).

seaweedfs.archNote: Upstream's index also carries 386 and arm/v7. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: ldflags are upstream's release workflow at 4.48 (binaries_release0.yml: -s -w -extldflags -static -X weed/util/version.COMMIT). The version NUMBER is compiled in from weed/util/version/constants.go, not stamped, so the Containerfile's version grep also proves the source constants agree with the ref. COMMIT is the pinned shortCommit, as upstream's container image stamps it. No build tags: the standard build (30GB volumes), not 5BytesOffset (large_disk), whose volume files a standard build cannot read -- switching later is a data migration, not a rebuild. -trimpath is ours. Only the Go weed binary ships; upstream's image also carries an optional Rust volume server and maintenance worker.

crosscheck.note: Upstream's own image (Alpine 3.23, ENTRYPOINT /entrypoint.sh, CMD mini -dir=/data, unsigned), per-platform children of the 4.51 index sha256:f7a49e3f... resolved 2026-10-28. best-effort: upstream builds without -trimpath on golang:1.26-alpine with a floating patch, so a byte mismatch is expected and proves nothing.

runtime.configNote: CMD is ours, not upstream's `mini` (which also opens an admin UI and WebDAV): a single-node master + volume + filer + S3 gateway, so the image runs standalone. Real deployments pass their own flags and an -s3.config identity file; without one the S3 gateway is open to anonymous requests.

seaweedfs.reason: Initial pin. Replaces MinIO, whose public images (quay.io/minio/minio, docker.io/minio/minio) answer 401 since 2026-10-07, as the S3 blob store of Sonatype Nexus. The vendor image is Alpine and unsigned; no UBI-based SeaweedFS exists. Built from source onto ubi9-micro. Onboarded in observe per adding-an-upstream.md. Licence Apache-2.0; unmodified and run internally. Consumer: infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack terraform/live/nexus-uar (PLAN-SeaweedFS.md Part A).

prometheus-nats-exporter.archNote: Upstream's index also carries arm/v6 and arm/v7. We build linux/amd64 and linux/arm64 only.

build.note: Flags are upstream's .goreleaser.yml at v0.20.2: -trimpath, -s -w, CGO_ENABLED=0, -X main.version={{.Version}} (the ref WITHOUT its v; the vendor binary prints `prometheus-nats-exporter version 0.20.2`). goreleaser's -X main.commit and -X main.date name symbols main.go does not declare, so they stamp nothing and are left out.

crosscheck.note: Upstream's own image (Alpine, ENTRYPOINT /entrypoint.sh exec'ing /prometheus-nats-exporter -> /usr/local/bin/prometheus-nats-exporter), per-platform children of the 0.20.2 index sha256:c623b608... resolved 2026-10-12. Checked for a signature, found none: `cosign download signature` -> no signatures associated; `cosign tree` -> no supply-chain artifacts. Hence trust class none. best-effort: the vendor binary reports go1.26.6 and -trimpath, while ours is built with toolchains.go1.26.goVersion (1.26.9 since 2026-10-13), and goreleaser's environment (GOAMD64, buildvcs) is not pinned data, so a byte mismatch proves nothing.

runtime.configNote: Stateless; no config file. CMD is upstream's `--help`, so the image runs standalone and exits. Deployments pass the endpoint flags and the NATS monitoring URL as the positional argument (e.g. `-varz -connz -subz -healthz -jsz=all http://127.0.0.1:8222`).

prometheus-nats-exporter.reason: Initial pin. No UBI-based exporter exists: the vendor image is Alpine and unsigned. Built from source onto ubi9-micro. Onboarded in observe per adding-an-upstream.md; moved to enforce 2026-10-14 after its first review on a pcre2-patched ubi9-micro (PR #32) came back clean on both arches: allow=true, blocking=0, waived=0, recorded=0, namespace trusted, so no exception was needed. Licence Apache-2.0. Consumer: infrashift/ansible-collection-infrashift-hashistack terraform/live/nats (a sidecar behind an mTLS metrics door; PLAN-SSHadowForge-Dashboards-20261012.md Part A/B, the deferred E5 of PLAN-SSHadowForge-Review-20261012.md).

packages.note: Exact NEVRAs, per architecture: PGDG can publish a different release on each (17.7 was 3PGDG.rhel9.6 on x86_64 and 2PGDG.rhel9 on aarch64). `track` bounds the VERSION-RELEASE of every pinned NEVRA to the 17 major line of the EL9 builds; scripts/drift-upstream.sh proposes the newest version-release in the repository that matches it, for every package and both architectures together. postgresql17 carries psql, pg_isready and createdb, which HALO and Chit run inside the container; postgresql17-libs is libpq; postgresql17-contrib carries pgcrypto, which Chit's first migration creates (the Docker and DHI images ship contrib too). contrib links libperl and libpython for its PL transform modules, so the perl and python3 runtime libraries come with it: on 2026-11-14 that added Mediums and one unfixable High (python3-pip-wheel), and no fixable finding. UBI dependencies (systemd-libs, libicu, krb5-libs and others) resolve at build time from the Red Hat signed UBI repositories and are recorded in the SBOM.

runtime.note: The environment contract of the Docker official and DHI postgres images, which HALO and Chit use today. UID 26 is the RHEL postgres user; its primary group is GID 0. The volume is mounted at /var/lib/pgsql/data and the cluster is in its userdata/ subdirectory, as in the Red Hat images. See images/postgresql17 in the wiki for what each consumer changes.

postgresql17.reason: Replaces the DHI postgres mirror for PostgreSQL 17 (owner decision 2026-11-14). The DHI 17 legs had 144 blocking Debian base findings that only Docker can clear; this image is PGDG's signed RPMs on our own ubi9-minimal, so its CVE surface is Red Hat's UBI content. The key is postgresql17, not postgresql with a 17 variant: a build-kind entry has one implicit variant, and one repository per major makes a major upgrade -- a dump and restore, never an image swap -- impossible to receive from a tag move. It does not collide with the mirror key `postgres`, which stays until HALO and Chit move.

native.note: gcc, make and openssl-devel come from the Red Hat signed UBI repositories in the builder; openssl (the CLI) only signs the throwaway certificate of the TLS smoke test, and pkgconf-pkg-config lets the Makefile find libssl. BUILD_TLS=yes links the UBI OpenSSL dynamically (HALO needs TLS); jemalloc and Lua come from Valkey's own deps/ tree. USE_SYSTEMD=no: a container has no systemd to notify. The binaries are stripped of debug data (--strip-debug keeps the symbol table for the crash report). valkey-check-aof, valkey-check-rdb and valkey-sentinel are symlinks to valkey-server, as in Valkey's own install; USE_REDIS_SYMLINKS=no, so no redis-* names.

runtime.note: Ours, not upstream's. Arguments passed to the container are appended to the config and override it: `--save "" --appendonly no` turns persistence off, `--requirepass` or an ACL file opens the network. Protected mode stays on, so with no password Valkey refuses every non-loopback client. The data directory is /data, owned by 1001:0 with g=u.

valkey.reason: Initial pin for HALO (P-TSC-6): Valkey is HALO's shared cache and state store, and LiteLLM's router and rate-limit store. Built in this repository (ADR-010): no free signed EL9 package exists, the vendor image is unsigned, and DHI Valkey had two Debian Criticals with no fix. Onboarded in observe.

native.note: Python 3.12 from UBI9 AppStream (python3.12-3.12.15-1.el9_8 on 2026-11-15); pip (python3.12-pip) only in the builder. The lock is generated from locks/litellm/requirements.in (litellm[proxy]==1.109.1 and redis) with uv --only-binary :all: --generate-hashes --exclude-newer 2026-11-15T00:00:00Z for Python 3.12 on manylinux_2_34; the same 117-wheel lock serves amd64 and arm64. pip installs it with --require-hashes --no-deps --only-binary=:all: into a venv created --without-pip, so the venv holds exactly the lock. No Prisma and no Node.js: the database features are out of scope (ADR-010).

runtime.note: Ours. The default config has no model and takes the master key from LITELLM_MASTER_KEY; mount a config to add models and the Redis (Valkey) router settings. LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True: the model cost map comes from the wheel, not from GitHub at start. The health endpoints /health/liveliness and /health/liveness need no key. The entrypoint (rootfs/litellm/usr/local/bin/litellm-entrypoint.sh) refuses to start when LITELLM_MASTER_KEY is unset or empty (owner's decision, 2026-11-15), then runs `litellm` with the arguments unchanged.

litellm.reason: Initial pin for HALO: LiteLLM is the OpenAI-compatible gateway to the model providers. Built in this repository by the owner's decision of 2026-11-15 (ADR-010), not mirrored from DHI: the DHI image's four blocking findings were all in its bundled Node.js, which this image does not carry. 1.109.1 is the newest LiteLLM release that is not a pre-release (2026-11-12). Onboarded in observe.

native.note: Every build package comes from the Red Hat signed UBI repositories in the builder. The commit has no configure script, so autoconf, automake and libtool generate it (./autogen.sh, as the vendor's `make dist` does); openssl (the CLI) only makes the throwaway certificate of the TLS smoke test. ./configure --with-openssl --without-cares --without-pam --without-ldap --without-systemd: TLS links the UBI OpenSSL dynamically (client_tls_* and server_tls_* work); DNS goes through libevent's evdns, because no UBI or PGDG repository ships c-ares (the PGDG RPM needs it, so the package kind cannot install PgBouncer); no PAM (pam-devel is not in UBI), no LDAP and no systemd notify. CFLAGS and LDFLAGS add the arch-neutral part of the RHEL hardening set (_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2, stack protector, stack-clash protection, PIE, full RELRO); only the `pgbouncer` make target is built. The runtime needs only libevent and openssl-libs, which ubi9-minimal already carries. No man pages: pandoc is not in UBI. The binary is stripped of debug data (--strip-debug keeps the symbol table).

runtime.note: Binary /usr/bin/pgbouncer; UID 1001 with primary GID 0 (PgBouncer refuses to run as root); entrypoint `pgbouncer`, default argument /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini, so `docker run /path/other.ini` uses another file. Ours, not upstream's: the default listens on *:6432, has no unix socket, no database, and an empty auth file (/etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt), so it starts but nobody can log in. HALO mounts its own pgbouncer.ini, auth file and TLS files over /etc/pgbouncer (or elsewhere and passes the path). Logs go to stderr. No volume: PgBouncer keeps no state.

pgbouncer.reason: Initial pin for HALO: the PostgreSQL connection pooler in front of postgresql17 in production. Built in this repository (ADR-010) because the package kind cannot install it: the PGDG EL9 pgbouncer RPM requires c-ares, which no UBI 9 or PGDG repository ships (checked 2026-11-15 on both architectures). Onboarded in observe.
